subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core enforce a Telegram/ACP source-turn action-verification or fail-closed policy for visible success claims, or should this issue be narrowed to delivery diagnostics while broad claim verification stays in plugin/ClawHub scope?
rationale: Current main documents and warns for only a narrower message_tool_only delivery miss, while a general success-claim verifier is a product/privacy/compatibility policy that VISION.md and the closed related proposal point toward plugins unless core needs a missing seam.

options.title: Define a narrow core source-turn invariant
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify which Telegram/ACP visible success claims require tool-ledger evidence and whether the outcome is warning, retry, suppression, or user-visible diagnostic.

options.title: Scope core to stranded delivery only
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85714 and its recovery PR for missing message-tool finals, and document that arbitrary claim verification is plugin-owned.

options.title: Close as plugin policy after documenting hooks
options.body: If maintainers decide this is entirely claim-verification policy, close this issue with the ClawHub/plugin handoff used for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/68051.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core source-turn invariant
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify which Telegram/ACP visible success claims require tool-ledger evidence and whether the outcome is warning, retry, suppression, or user-visible diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest evidence trail on both the source-reply warning policy and the prior claim-verification product-boundary decision.
